verdict.line: You lose if you let Mordekaiser stack his passive on you in extended trades; you win if you poke with Q and disengage before he gets three hits off.

brief.thesis: This is a near-coinflip on the numbers (50.6% over 2157 games) but the lane itself is structurally uncomfortable: Mordekaiser's passive, Darkness Rise, rewards him for landing three hits on you in a single engagement, and Gangplank has no dash or gap-closer to control when that engagement happens. Your entire plan is to make him pay for every stack with Q (Parrrley) poke rather than letting him pick the fight on his terms.

theirWindow.when: he has 2+ passive stacks on you
theirWindow.what: Disengage immediately. His third hit grants the damage aura and move speed burst, and staying in range to auto-trade here just feeds the proc you're trying to avoid.

yourWindow.when: his E (Death's Grasp) is on cooldown (16-8s)
yourWindow.what: Step up and land Q (Parrrley) freely. Without E he has no way to pull you back into range after you poke, so this is your lowest-risk window to chip him down.

start.why: The sustain and early AD let you win extended auto-trades against his point-and-click Q (Obliterate) without needing to all-in.

boots.why: The lifesteal directly offsets the magic damage he piles on through autos and Obliterate, and it's the higher win-rate pick in this matchup (56.9% over 629 games).

core.why: Mana sustain lets you spam Q (Parrrley) poke every cooldown without running dry, which is how you actually win trades here
Execute threshold turns your poke damage into kills once he's been whittled down
He builds toward Indestructible stacks and raw HP, and the armor pen cuts straight through that

situational.when: he rushes Indestructible or any shield-heavy build to blunt your poke
you're ahead and want to close out fights faster instead of grinding him down

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards your poke-and-walk-away pattern with burn damage that doesn't require you to stay in his passive-stacking range

summoners.why: Ignite punishes his lack of sustain outside Indestructible's shield, and this pairing has the highest win rate and by far the highest pick rate (50.7% over 88.3% of games) for this matchup.

playing.title: Poke with Q, never auto-chain
playing.detail: Land Parrrley and walk back. Standing still to auto-trade is exactly how he racks up the three hits needed for Darkness Rise.

playing.title: Save W for his R
playing.detail: Remove Scurvy clears crowd control, but more importantly it's your out once Realm of Death locks you in. Don't burn it early just to heal off chip damage.

playing.title: Track his E cooldown
playing.detail: Death's Grasp drops from 16s to 8s as he levels it. Once he's rank 3-5, he can punish overextension on a much shorter timer, so tighten your leash in lane accordingly.

playing.title: Never all-in off cooldown
playing.detail: This is a defensive-shape matchup by design (OP.GG flags avoiding prolonged combat). Your damage comes from poke volume over 15 minutes, not a single all-in window.

playing.title: Use E for wave clear and siege
playing.detail: Raise Morale doesn't help you win the 1v1 directly, but the attack speed and move speed let you shove faster and reset back to safety before he can engage.

playing.title: Respect his ultimate from level 6
playing.detail: Realm of Death removes you from the lane and steals your stats if he kills you in it. Don't get caught overextended past minion range once he's 6.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win rates are pulled from measured OP.GG data on the current patch (16.19.1); the tactical reasoning on passive stacks, cooldown windows, and trade patterns is my own read of the matchup.

stats.opponentTip: Get rid of Mordekaiser’s (R) with [W]. Gain stacks of Grasp of the Undying while avoid fighting in prolonged combat.
